item.title: Atiku wanted me as running mate in 2023 – Makinde
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has revealed that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar approached him to be his running mate in the 2023 presidential election, but he declined the offer because he considered himself inexperienced in public service at the time. Makinde disclosed this during an interview on ARISE News, where he spoke about his political journey, his relationship with members of the G5 governors, the crisis within the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and his political ambitions. The governor said he was approached to run alongside Atiku but turned down the offer, explaining that he had only spent three years in office as governor of Oyo State. He said, “Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and his people approached me to run with him. I basically told them that I had only spent three years as governor of Oyo State and three years in public service. I felt it was not enough to make such a decision, so I told them to look for someone else.” Speaking on the G5 governors’ decision to oppose Atiku’s presidential ambition in 2023, Makinde said he was the only member of the group who had since left the PDP. He also defended the decision by his faction to expel former Rivers State Governor Nyesom Wike from the party, saying it was necessary after Wike declared his intention to hold the PDP for President Bola Tinubu. Makinde said the decision was aimed at allowing the party to participate in the election, even if it meant going to the polls with a weakened structure. He, however, expressed concern over the state of Nigeria’s democracy, questioning why political parties were still dealing with the nullification of candidates less than 80 days before a national election. “Why? What kind of democracy is that?” he asked. Reacting to allegations by the Oyo State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he had abandoned governance to pursue his political campaign, Makinde defended his activities outside the state. He argued that if the President could travel around the country for political activities, governors should also be allowed to take their messages to Nigerians. Makinde maintained that governance in Oyo State had continued despite his political engagements, citing his presentation of the 2027 budget estimates to the State House of Assembly and his state-of-the-state address. “Oyo State is moving on. We have robust institutions, and I am not outside the country,” he said. On his preferred successor, Bimbo Adekanbi, Makinde dismissed suggestions that his support for the former commissioner made him a political godfather. He explained that Adekanbi emerged through a consensus process which he supported, but insisted that his successor should be allowed to establish his own political identity. “I have told him severally, ‘Bimbo, don’t inherit my enemies or opponents. item.title: 2027: My presidential bid may have upset Tinubu — Makinde
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate Seyi Makinde says he believes his presidential ambition may have caused “bad blood” between him and President Bola Tinubu, whom he supported in the 2023 election, adding that he could only speculate that people may have told Tinubu he was also considering a run. Makinde made the remarks during an interview with Arise Television on Friday, while discussing how his relationship with Tinubu changed after he helped the President win votes in Oyo State in 2023. He also recalled meeting Tinubu when the FCT Minister Nyesom Wike told him he would hold the PDP for him ahead of the 2027 elections. “Well, I can only guess. Yes, please. You know, people talk a lot. Maybe some people went and told him, ‘Look, Seyi may likely run against you.’ I don’t know. That may cause bad blood between us,” Makinde said. “We were with the president and the minister of FCT. You know, knelt just by his side and told him that, look, I will hold PDP for you.” Makinde also said he supported Wike during the 2023 PDP presidential primary which meant he could not have been driven by an ambition to run. He added that he had also declined an approach from former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s associates to join him on a ticket in 2023, saying he had not been governor or a public servant long enough to take on the role. He added: “So, it was my ambition, but I supported him in 2023 during the presidential primary of PDP. So, I didn’t have ambition then. I suddenly just developed an ambition. And let me say this: former VP Atiku Abubakar had his people approach me to run with him, and I basically told them, ‘Look, I was only three years as a governor in Oyo State, and three years as a public servant. So it wasn’t enough to take such a decision.’ So I said to them, ‘No, go look for someone else that can run. If it’s an ambition driving me, that is probably the surest part.” Makinde also said Tinubu did not contact him during the 56 days pupils and teachers abducted in Oriire Local Government Area remained in captivity. He said he had tried to see the President because he expected him to show concern over the kidnapping. “I tried to see the President when our students and our children and their teachers were kidnapped, because I thought if any part of Nigeria is going through such a challenge, the president should be interested. Actually, I expected the president to call me,” he said. Asked whether Tinubu eventually contacted him, Makinde replied: “He did not. No. Till tomorrow.” The governor said he also tried to reach the President through the State Chief of Protocol but received no response. He said he had never spoken directly with Tinubu about anything and was focused on governing Oyo State. “I’m saying it again that till tomorrow I’ve not spoken directly with the President about anything. item.title: Ogun 2027: PDP celebrates Adebutu ruling, vows to reclaim state
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Following a fresh boost to Hon. Ladi Adebutu’s candidacy, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has vowed to reclaim Ogun State in the 2027 governorship election, urging residents to rally behind its candidate and other party flag-bearers. The party made the declaration while reacting to a Federal High Court judgment ordering the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to reinstate Adebutu as its governorship candidate, saying the ruling had strengthened its determination to return to power in the state. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, the PDP welcomed the judgment as a victory for democracy, justice and the rule of law. The party said the development had energised its members, supporters and stakeholders as it intensified preparations for the 2027 general elections. It urged the people of Ogun State to rally behind Adebutu and other PDP candidates, promising a government focused on economic opportunities, infrastructure, education and healthcare. “Our desire and commitment is to build an Ogun state where economic opportunities are expanded, infrastructure is strengthened, education and healthcare receive the attention they deserve, and government genuinely serves the interests of the people,” Jungudo said. The PDP expressed confidence that a fresh mandate from Ogun residents would enable it to pursue the state’s developmental aspirations and improve the living conditions of its citizens. “The journey to reclaim Ogun State and restore purposeful governance is firmly on course,” the party declared. item.title: Attack on NDC supporters in Lagos cowardly — Ladipo Johnson
item.description: Mr Ladipo Johnson, Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Lagos Central Senatorial candidate, has described the attack on supporters of the party in Lagos as cowardly, premeditated and unprovoked. Johnson made the condemnation in Lagos on Friday, while reacting to the disruption of the party’s town hall meeting at the Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that NDC supporters had gathered at the venue ahead of a town hall meeting with the party’s presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. Johnson said the incident should not be regarded as a feud between political groups, stressing that those attacked were law-abiding citizens exercising their democratic rights. “First, let me clarify that what transpired yesterday along Kudirat Abiola Way in Oregun, Ikeja, was not a feud. A feud implies a mutual dispute between two parties. “What we witnessed yesterday was a premeditated, unprovoked and cowardly attack on peaceful, law-abiding citizens and supporters of the NDC,” he said. He said the incident was deeply troubling and reflected growing concerns about political intimidation and violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. Johnson called on political leaders to be mindful of their public statements, arguing that inflammatory rhetoric could embolden supporters to resort to violence. “We must call a spade a spade. The audacity displayed by these hoodlums does not exist in a vacuum. When the leadership of a nation uses rhetoric that frames power as something to ‘grab, snatch and run with’, it sends a dangerous signal,” he said. He called on President Bola Tinubu to personally address Nigerians and condemn the incident, urging him to direct state governors and security agencies to take decisive measures against political violence. “It is simply not enough for the All Progressives Congress (APC) to issue routine statements distancing itself from the violence. “If the administration is truly committed to democracy and the rule of law, President Tinubu must personally address the nation, unequivocally condemn yesterday’s attack and read the riot act to state governors, the Inspector-General of Police and the heads of all security agencies,” he said. Johnson warned that failure to take decisive action could undermine public confidence in the government’s commitment to protecting democratic rights. He maintained that the incident would not discourage the NDC from exercising its constitutional rights or engaging voters across Lagos State. “If the intention behind yesterday’s attack was to instil fear in our supporters or disrupt our momentum in Lagos, it has failed woefully. “The NDC and the broader opposition will not be cowed. We will stand our ground whenever and wherever we are attacked or intimidated,” he said. item.title: How Flamingos Ended Africa’s Long Wait For Women’s World Cup Glory
item.description: For decades, African football has produced teams capable of challenging the world’s best, but winning a FIFA World Cup title has remained an elusive ambition for the continent’s women’s national teams. That long wait finally ended on Saturday, November 7, 2026, when Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, conquered the world in Morocco. A hard-fought 2-1 victory over Japan in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup secured Nigeria’s maiden title in the competition and made the Flamingos the first African women’s national team to win a FIFA World Cup trophy at any level. Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku, scored in the 39th and 47th minutes respectively, gave Nigeria a two-goal advantage before Japan’s Fuki Ito reduced the deficit in the 80th minute. The Nigerian girls, however, showed remarkable composure under pressure to protect their lead and write their names into football history. It was a victory that meant considerably more than another trophy for Nigeria. It represented a breakthrough for African women’s football and demonstrated that the continent’s young talents could go all the way against the established powers of the game. ﻿ A Journey Defined By Resilience The road to the trophy was far from straightforward. The Flamingos began their campaign with a disappointing 2-1 defeat to Poland, raising questions about their readiness to compete for the title. However, rather than allow the setback to derail their ambitions, the Nigerian girls responded with character and determination, winning their remaining six matches to complete a remarkable turnaround. They returned to winning ways with a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the biggest statements of the tournament by defeating defending champions North Korea 3-1. The result ended the Asian side’s 18-match unbeaten run in regulation time at the competition and announced Nigeria as a serious contender. The Flamingos maintained their momentum in the knockout stages, defeating Mexico 2-1 in the Round of 16. Oluebube Umejiaku and Mary Dunstan found the net to send Nigeria into the quarter-finals. Azeezat Oduntan then emerged as the match-winner against Venezuela, converting a late penalty in the 89th minute to secure a 1-0 victory and book Nigeria’s place in the last four. Their biggest test arguably came in the semi-finals against Brazil. But the Flamingos delivered an emphatic performance, defeating the South Americans 3-1 to reach their first-ever final at the competition. Queen Joseph opened the scoring in the 56th minute before Awawu Bashiru struck twice, in the 71st and 80th minutes, to put Nigeria firmly in control. Brazil managed a late consolation, but it was not enough to prevent the Nigerian side from securing a historic place in the final. item.title: 2027: Immigration vows to block foreign mercenaries, illicit arms
item.description: The Nigeria Immigration Service NIS has pledged to tighten surveillance at the nation’s borders ahead of the 2027 general election, as sister security agencies named foreign mercenaries and illicit arms among the threats it must help keep out of the electoral process. Comptroller General of the Immigration Service, Kemi Nana Nandap, made the pledge on Friday in Abuja at a sensitisation workshop on election security for senior personnel, themed “The strategic role of the NIS in Election Monitoring and intimidation”. “As we prepare for the 2027 general elections, let us be guided by the common purpose to protect our national security, uphold the rule of law, and contribute to an electoral environment in which every Nigerian can exercise their democratic rights peacefully and without intimidation.” Represented by the Deputy Comptroller General DCG in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, the immigration boss said, “As the agency charged with the mandate of border security and migration management, we occupy a strategic position in the nation’s security architecture. We must therefore remain alert to the influx of foreigners, particularly irregular migration, trafficking in persons, smuggling of migrants, and other transnational criminal activities capable of undermining national security.” The Comptroller General stressed that the service cannot do this alone. “No single agency can address the complex security challenges confronting our nation in isolation,” the address said, appreciating “the continued partnership” of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC and other security agencies. Warning the personnel against partisanship, the immigration boss said, “Let us therefore reiterate that the Nigeria Immigration Service remains a non-partisan institution. Under no circumstances should our personnel use official resources to promote partisan interests. “You must ensure that our commands are adequately prepared before, during, and after elections through strengthening surveillance, intelligence gathering, effective deployment, and close coordination with relevant security agencies,” she said. In inter-agency work, the CG said the service’s participation in the Interagency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES must be proactive, purposeful, and result-orientated. “I expect every senior officer to lead by example and take full responsibility for maintaining professional standards within their respective formats,” she stated. In his remarks, Director General, Department of State Services DSS, Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi told the gathering that electoral periods attract attempts to exploit the nation’s frontiers for the movement of “illicit arms, mercenaries” and others bent on undermining the democratic process. item.title: Iran seeks stronger economic, political ties with Nigeria
item.description: Iranian President Dr Masoud Pezeshkian has underscored the need to deepen Nigeria-Iran economic, political and cultural ties to harness untapped potential and enhance bilateral cooperation between both countries. Pezeshkian ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌‌⁠⁠‌‍‌‌​said this while receiving the Letters of Credence presented to him by Nigeria’s Ambassador to Iran, Amb. Hamza Sallau, during an official diplomatic engagement in Tehran. This is contained in a statement issued on Friday in Abuja by Mr Oluwafemi Adeniyi, spokesperson for Nigeria’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. He reiterated Iran’s commitment to identifying and pursuing new opportunities aimed at strengthening diplomatic relations and delivering mutually beneficial outcomes for both countries. Earlier, Sallau conveyed the warm greetings of President Bola Tinubu to President Pezeshkian and the people of Iran, reaffirming Nigeria’s commitment to deepening bilateral relations. According to him, trade, agriculture and healthcare are priority areas for enhanced collaboration between the two countries to promote economic growth and strengthen cooperation. The envoy commended both countries’ shared commitment to multilateralism and international cooperation, saying the Nigeria-Iran Joint Commission should be prioritised as a mechanism to advance bilateral cooperation. He added that the commission should identify new practical areas for mutually beneficial partnerships between the two countries, while strengthening existing diplomatic and economic ties. Both parties restated their commitment to expanding political engagement, strengthening institutional cooperation and promoting people-to-people relations between Nigeria and Iran. The presentation of the Letters of Credence by Sallau formally marked his accreditation as Nigeria’s Ambassador Plenipotentiary and Extraordinary to the Islamic Republic of Iran. It also reflects Nigeria’s continued commitment to pursuing mutually beneficial relations with Iran in furtherance of its foreign policy objectives. item.title: Pochettino poised to agree 2.5-year deal at Man Utd
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino is set to agree a two-and-a-half-year deal to take charge of beleaguered Manchester United following the sacking of Michael Carrick, reports said Friday. The Athletic said an agreement had been reached with the USA head coach over a contract that would keep the 54-year-old at Old Trafford until 2029. Pochettino is set to take charge of his team’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final ties against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday before heading to Manchester. An announcement on his future could come as early as Friday, with the Argentinian set to hold a press conference previewing the first leg against Haiti at 1415 GMT. US Soccer is understood to have accepted that Pochettino is stepping down. The federation is set to receive $10 million in compensation for him plus a further $2 million for the departure of his coaching staff. Carrick was dismissed on Thursday following intense speculation over his future after a disastrous start to the season. The 20-time English champions are in the relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 matches in the Premier League so far. Carrick, who won multiple trophies as a midfielder in the club’s golden era under Alex Ferguson, is the seventh permanent manager to be dismissed by the club since the Scot retired in 2013. Pochettino guided World Cup co-hosts the USA to the last 16 of the tournament earlier this year before signing a contract extension taking him through to the 2030 World Cup. He has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. One early issue for Pochettino to wrestle with could be the future of United captain Bruno Fernandes, who has been the club’s outstanding performer for many seasons. The Portuguese attacking midfielder is understood to have rejected a second contract offer. The Red Devils have an option to extend his deal to the end of the 2027/2028 season, meaning he would not be free to talk to other clubs in January. item.title: COREN Commends Nile university as 261 Engineering graduates take professional oath
item.description: Nile University of Nigeria has inducted 261 graduates of its Faculty of Engineering into the Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE) and administered the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN) oath in its maiden Induction and Oath-Taking Ceremony, as the institution intensifies efforts to align its programmes with international standards. The ceremony marks a significant milestone for the University’s Faculty of Engineering, which was established in 2009 and has grown into one of its flagship academic units, offering programmes in Civil Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, and Petroleum and Gas Engineering. Prof. Prema A. Kirubakaran, who represented the Vice-Chancellor, described the ceremony as a landmark achievement for the Faculty and urged the newly inducted engineers to uphold the values of integrity, responsibility and continuous learning throughout their careers. Delivering the keynote address, Engr. Dr. Adamu Muhammed, MNSE, MNSChE, PMP, AMIChemE, Terminal Manager, NNPC Limited, praised Nile University of Nigeria for its contribution to engineering education, describing the institution as one capable of standing alongside leading universities globally. He challenged the new engineers to remain honest, continue learning and apply their knowledge to solving Nigeria’s developmental challenges. He urged the graduates to build careers defined by innovation, discipline and professional excellence. Speaking at the ceremony, Engr. Prof. Okorie Austine Uchegbusi Uche, FNSE, Registrar of COREN, commended Nile University of Nigeria for its implementation of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), describing it as one of the few institutions in the country actively applying the approach, which emphasises measurable competencies and graduate outcomes. Reflecting on the significance of the occasion, the Dean of the Faculty of Engineering, Engr. Prof. Abdulhameed Danjuma Mambo, said the induction signified the graduates’ readiness to assume the responsibilities of professional engineering practice. “Graduation shows that you have learned, but induction shows that you have become a professional,” he said. According to him, while members of the public may never see the calculations behind engineering projects, they place their trust in the professionalism and judgment of engineers responsible for them. Prof. Mambo said the Faculty remains committed to producing graduates equipped with the technical knowledge, professional values and practical skills required to contribute to national development. He noted that the ongoing accreditation activities involving the Faculty form part of efforts to ensure that its programmes meet global standards and remain competitive internationally. item.title: Is Galadima the Round Peg in the Round Hole for Adamawa?
item.description: In Nigerian politics, the phrase “a round peg in a round hole” is often used to suggest that a candidate’s temperament, experience and timing align perfectly with the demands of the moment. In Adamawa State, that description is increasingly being attached to Ahmed Tijjani Galadima, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for 2027. But is he truly the right fit for Adamawa’s complex political and developmental realities, or simply the beneficiary of strategic party consensus? Adamawa is no ordinary political battleground. Situated in Nigeria’s North-East, the state has long balanced agricultural potential with security challenges, urban expansion with rural neglect, and a politically vibrant electorate with shifting party loyalties. Governorship contests here are rarely predictable. Personal networks, regional considerations, grassroots mobilisation and elite consensus all play decisive roles—and often collide. Galadima’s emergence as the APC’s standard-bearer was no accident. A seasoned technocrat, he previously served as Executive Secretary of the Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a position that placed him at the intersection of public administration, human capital development and federal policymaking. Within policy circles, that experience is often cited as evidence of administrative competence—a quality many voters say has become increasingly important after years of governance characterised more by political brinkmanship than institutional reform. Within the APC, his candidacy also represents consolidation. Several key aspirants stepped aside before and during the primary process, sparing the party the bruising internal contest that has weakened it in previous election cycles. For a party seeking to reclaim power in Adamawa from the administration of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, unity is more than desirable; it is essential. Galadima’s ability to attract support across competing blocs suggests he enjoys both political goodwill and strategic alliances. Yet politics in Adamawa extends beyond party arithmetic. The electorate remains deeply concerned about security, particularly in communities affected by the spillover of insurgency in the North-East. Farmers want safer farmlands, traders need secure transport corridors, and young people seek economic opportunities that do not require leaving the state. Any candidate seeking to be regarded as the “right fit” must present credible solutions to these interconnected challenges. Supporters argue that Galadima’s administrative experience positions him to drive economic renewal. Adamawa’s economy remains largely agrarian, with significant untapped potential in agro-processing, livestock production and cross-border trade with neighbouring Cameroon. With improved infrastructure, targeted investment incentives and better access to rural finance, the state could move beyond subsistence agriculture towards value-added production. item.title: Nigerian Microbiologist Bridget Ugochi Anyanwueze develops improved laboratory method to advance antimicrobial drug discovery and research
item.description: Her research introduces a time-dependent approach to measuring bacterial inhibition, offering additional information that could support the laboratory evaluation of potential antimicrobial compounds. As antimicrobial resistance continues to threaten global health, researchers are investigating new compounds capable of inhibiting bacterial growth and improving the laboratory methods used to evaluate their activity. Among these efforts is the research of microbiologist Bridget Ugochi Anyanwueze, whose work examines how antibiotic inhibition zones develop over time and how these measurements could contribute to future antimicrobial investigations. Her sole-authored research paper, “An Improved in vitro Method for Quantifying the Kinetics of Bacterial Inhibition-Zone Development,” was published on June 27, 2026, in the IPS Journal of Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology, with link to article https://doi.org/10.54117/ijamb.v6i2.170 . The study was conducted within her broader research interests in microbiology and antimicrobial activity, with her affiliation listed as the Department of Biology at Southeast Missouri State University, Cape Girardeau, United States. The research addresses a limitation of the traditional Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion assay, a laboratory method used to assess bacterial susceptibility to antibiotics. Traditionally, the method measures the diameter of the clear zone surrounding an antibiotic disc after a specified incubation period. Although this measurement provides important information about bacterial susceptibility, it does not describe how the inhibition zone develops during the preceding hours. Anyanwueze investigated whether repeated measurements could provide additional information about the progression of bacterial inhibition. Using Staphylococcus epidermidis as the test organism, she examined inhibition-zone development following exposure to ampicillin, erythromycin, and neomycin. Measurements were collected at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 25 hours of incubation, allowing changes in inhibition-zone diameter and expansion rate to be examined over time. The findings revealed that the antibiotics exhibited different patterns of inhibition-zone development. Ampicillin produced the greatest absolute increase in inhibition-zone diameter, expanding by 10.23 millimetres, while erythromycin demonstrated the highest percentage expansion at 137.9%. The study also found that inhibition zones generally expanded more rapidly during earlier observations before slowing at later incubation intervals. These differences demonstrate that final inhibition-zone diameters do not capture every aspect of how inhibition zones develop. By incorporating repeated measurements, the improved approach provides additional quantitative information about the progression of measurable bacterial growth inhibition. item.title: We won’t jump to conclusions over NDC attack – Lagos APC
item.description: The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) says it will not jump to conclusions or make needless assumptions over the disruption of a political gathering organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Ikeja. The party’s spokesman, Mr Seye Oladejo, said this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) while responding to questions on the alleged attack on NDC members and the party’s denial of involvement in the incident. Oladejo said APC was a party governed by the principles of law and order and would not engage in speculative conclusions over the circumstances surrounding the incident. “We’re a party governed by law and order. However, we won’t jump the gun and embark on needless assumptions,” he said. He, however, urged Nigerians not to overlook what he described as recent threats by opposition political parties to unleash mayhem in the state. “The threats to unleash mayhem by the opposition parties recently should not be lost on the public. “Our democracy cannot thrive on anarchy and disorderly conduct,” he said. Oladejo said the APC remained committed to democratic principles, peaceful political engagement and respect for the rule of law. He stressed that political competition should not be allowed to degenerate into violence, intimidation or activities capable of undermining democratic institutions. The spokesman urged political parties and their supporters to exercise restraint and conduct their activities within the ambit of the law, particularly as political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gathered momentum. He also reiterated the need for security agencies to remain vigilant and discharge their constitutional responsibilities to prevent threats to public peace. Oladejo said political differences should be resolved through lawful democratic processes rather than actions capable of creating tension and disorder. He maintained that the APC would continue to pursue its political activities through persuasion, issue-based campaigns, grassroots mobilisation and the ballot box. NAN reports that Lagos APC, in a statement on Thursday by Oladejo, denied allegations that it sponsored the disruption of an NDC political gathering in Ikeja. The party described the allegation as reckless, baseless and irresponsible, insisting that it neither sponsored, encouraged nor participated in any action capable of undermining the constitutional rights of opposition parties. It said the alleged incident occurred on the same day APC held the official flag-off of its 2027 general election campaign in Epe, several kilometres away from Ikeja. According to the statement, the party’s leaders, elected representatives, executives, campaign officials and other stakeholders were mobilised for the Epe event. APC also accused opposition political elements of making threats to unleash violence and render the political atmosphere ungovernable. item.title: 2027: We received phone call from Buhari’s grave to vote Atiku — Dalung
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A former Minister of Sports and Youth Development, Solomon Dalung, has claimed that supporters of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) received a phone call from the grave of former President Muhammadu Buhari, urging them to vote for the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the 2027 election. Dalung, an ADC chieftain, made the remark on Thursday while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he also linked the alleged message to a recent visit by Buhari’s widow, Aisha, to Atiku in Abuja. “Last month you saw when the wife of the late president visited Atiku in Abuja. The message she took for any politician to know is that the 12 million votes have been successfully transferred. We have had a phone call from the grave of Buhari that we should vote Atiku,” he said. Dalung argued that Atiku had inherited the political structures of both Buhari and former President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, giving him a nationwide political network. He also dismissed the possibility of President Bola Tinubu defeating Atiku in 2027, saying the ADC candidate would remain difficult to overcome even if the ruling party prevented the opposition from campaigning. “I am confident that as events are unfolding, Tinubu, even if he would take over the ADC secretariat and stop ADC from campaigning, he cannot defeat Atiku Abubakar in 2027,” he said. He alleged that President Tinubu is scared of 2027 election saying, “I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” he said. item.title: Tinubu’s govt using EFCC to blackmail governors into APC — Makinde alleges
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has accused the President Bola Tinubu-led administration of using the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to intimidate governors and pressure them into joining the ruling All Progressives Congress. Makinde, who spoke during an interview on Arise News on Friday, alleged that opposition governors who refuse to defect to the APC risk being subjected to investigations and blackmail, warning that the development could undermine Nigeria’s multiparty democracy. “What we’ve seen is, well, okay, I have the governors, they come to APC. If you don’t, you will be blackmailed,” Makinde said. To illustrate his claim, he described a situation in which a contractor working for an opposition-controlled state could face scrutiny over government contracts and financial transactions. “The EFCC will come down from that place. ‘Look, how much did they award this to you? Go and bring your account. Who have you been paying?’ That is the situation that we are facing today,” he said. Makinde also alleged that the Federal Government tried to blackmail him over the Bodija explosion intervention funds, saying his administration had already compensated affected property owners before receiving federal assistance. He said the state engaged the Nigerian Society of Engineers and valuers to assess the damage and determine payments to victims. “We’ve spent the money. We got Nigerian Society of Engineers. We got valuers. You know, they went out there, had valuation of the properties, and then we gave money back to those people, and we did it before even getting anything from the federal,” he said. He added that he released the state’s account of the transaction when the issue was raised and directed the Commissioner for Finance to channel the funds into projects. Makinde did not provide evidence during the interview that the president or the APC had directed the EFCC to investigate opposition governors or their contractors. item.title: 2027 Elections: My Loyalty Is Solely To The Constitution, Says INEC Chairman Amupitan
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, has declared that his loyalty is solely to the Nigerian Constitution and the Electoral Act, insisting that his leadership of the electoral body will remain impartial. Amupitan stated this n on Thursday while responding to questions about his neutrality at Chatham House, London, during a high-level dialogue organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI). The dialogue was held under the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” His comments followed the controversy that surrounded an X (formerly Twitter) account allegedly linked to him, which allegedly made a partisan post expressing support for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) during the 2023 general elections. INEC had, however, denied that Amupitan operated the account, describing the allegations as digital impersonation. Responding to the issue at Chatham House on Thursday, the INEC chairman denied operating an X account, saying an independent forensic review had been obtained and the matter formally referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Inspector-General of Police for investigation. Amupitan (right) spoke at Chatham House on Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Photo: X/@inecnigeria) Dismissing concerns about his impartiality, Amupitan said his allegiance was to the country’s legal framework rather than any political interest. “My loyalty is solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the Electoral Act,” he declared. “Every constitutional institution—including the Presidency, the National Assembly, and state governors—owes its primary loyalty to the Constitution and the rule of law.” The INEC chairman also dismissed suggestions that his previous legal representation in political disputes could compromise his neutrality, explaining that he acted strictly within his professional responsibilities as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria before his appointment. Amupitan urged Nigerians to trust his leadership to conduct free, fair, and credible elections in 2027, citing improvements recorded in recent off-cycle elections and technical safeguards introduced by the commission. He acknowledged that the controversies surrounding the 2023 presidential election had significantly damaged public confidence in INEC. “First and foremost, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC—damage so large that the Commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. He added that the commission had learnt lessons from subsequent elections, including those in Anambra and Osun states, where results were declared the day after voting. Meanwhile, Amupitan identified insecurity, logistics and result management as the commission’s major priorities ahead of the 2027 elections. item.title: Just in: Court orders INEC to publish Adebutu’s name as Ogun PDP gov candidate
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to, within 24 hours, publish Oladipupo Adebutu’s name as Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)’s candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgment, held that INEC had no powers to unilaterally remove the name of a validly nominated candidate by a political party. Justice Lifu held that the commission’s action was unconstitutional, unlawful and was of no effect. Justice Lifu said that it is only the Federal High Court or the state’s high court that has the power to declare a candidate invalid and not the commission. He held that INEC breached Adebutu’s right to fair hearing. The judge, who dismissed the preliminary objection filed by INEC, declared that the suit was competent. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the PDP and Adebutu had, on Oct. 22, filed the suit following the removal of Adebutu’s name from the list of contestants of the governorship seat in Ogun. The plaintiffs sued INEC as the sole defendant in the suit filed by their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, SAN. The plaintiffs, who sought six questions for determination, prayed the court for 11 reliefs. They sought an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10 for denial of a fair hearing and violation of the provisions of Section 29 and Section 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026. They also sought an order directing or compelling “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election,” among other reliefs. item.title: 2027: INEC rules out inaccurate IReV uploads
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has built strict validation safeguards into its system to prevent inaccurate results or figures reflecting over-voting from being uploaded to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). Thus is contained in a statement issued by the Chief Press Secretary to the INEC chairman, Mr Adedayo Oketola, in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja.’ Amupitan therefore urged Nigerians to trust his leadership to deliver free, fair and credible general elections in 2027. He highlighted measurable operational improvements recorded in recent off-cycle polls and new technical safeguards designed to prevent a repeat of the 2023 election controversies. On the trust deficit left by the 2023 presidential election, Amupitan acknowledged that the controversies surrounding that exercise severely dented public confidence in the electoral body. “First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC, damage so large that the commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said. Amupitan, who assumed office in October 2025, noted that INEC had treated every subsequent election as a practical laboratory to identify operational weaknesses and strengthen accreditation, voting and result management. Responding to a question on why Nigerians should trust his leadership ahead of 2027, he cited the successful conduct of recent off-cycle elections, including the Ekiti, Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, and 16 legislative bye-elections. “Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections, and observers agree that the recent election in Osun marked a clear improvement. “Every election is a lesson. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said. He noted that Anambra and Osun previously had histories of prolonged, inconclusive governorship contests, recalling that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude. He, however, said targeted administrative reforms under his watch enabled results in both states to be declared the day after voting. Highlighting insecurity, logistics and result management as INEC’s three top priorities for 2027, Amupitan revealed that the commission’s post-2023 audit traced the most acute result management failures to collation centres rather than polling units. item.title: Oriire: Tinubu never spoke to me over abducted pupils, teachers — Makinde
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has said President Bola Tinubu failed to contact him during the 56 days pupils and teachers abducted in the state remained in captivity, despite his efforts to reach the president. Makinde said he expected Tinubu to call or show concern over the incident, which involved the abduction of schoolchildren and their teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of the state. The governor made this known during an interview with Arise Television on Friday, while discussing his relationship with Tinubu, whom he supported in the 2023 presidential election. “I tried to see the President when our students and our children and their teachers were kidnapped, because I thought if any part of Nigeria is going through such a challenge, the president should be interested. Actually, I expected the president to call me,” he said. Asked whether Tinubu eventually contacted him, Makinde replied, “He did not. No. Till tomorrow.” The governor added that he also tried reaching the president through the State Chief of Protocol but received no response to his call. Makinde maintained that he had never spoken directly with Tinubu, stressing that he was focused on governing Oyo State. “I’m saying it again that till tomorrow I’ve not spoken directly with the President about anything. I’m just minding my own business, running Oyo State. And I’m not complaining,” he said. The governor’s remarks come months after the abducted pupils and teachers regained their freedom following 56 days in captivity. The victims were seized on May 15, 2026, when gunmen attacked schools in the area. The Nigerian Army announced their rescue on July 10 after a security operation involving multiple agencies. item.title: Makinde scores Tinubu administration 34 per cent
item.description: Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has scored President Bola Tinubu’s administration 34 per cent, saying the government has failed to secure the support of a majority of Nigerians. Makinde gave the assessment during an interview with Arise Television, where he was asked to evaluate the administration’s performance in infrastructure, diplomacy and economic growth. He likened the score to the percentage of Nigerians who supported Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, arguing that the President needed to win over those who voted against him to build a national consensus. “It’s just about the same percentage as the people that supported him in 2023, 34 per cent. You need the 66 per cent of Nigerians that were against him in 2023 to be on board. This is a national project,” he said. The governor also criticised what he described as pressure on elected officials to join the ruling All Progressives Congress, alleging that some governors were compelled to defect. “Look at what we’ve seen. You have the governors come to APC. If you don’t, you’ll be blackmailed,” he said. Makinde, who is seeking the presidency in 2027 under the Action Peoples Party (APM), also addressed whether he would accept defeat if the election was free, fair and credible. Responding to a question on whether he would concede defeat and retire to farming, the governor said he would accept the outcome if the electoral process met the required standards. “There are a few things that must happen. If the process is free, fair, and credible, yes, I will,” he said. However, when asked whether he would remain in the APM after the election, Makinde said his political future would depend on how Nigerians received his political agenda. “I may evaluate my political future depending on how Nigerians, you know, see this agenda,” he added. item.title: Meet Ilaro Poly graduate Tunji Adaramola leading power system rebuild on US self-driving car project
item.description: By Ayo Taiwo A Nigerian electrical engineer, Tunji Semiu Adaramola, has led the rebuild of a critical power panel on the autonomous electric vehicle developed by North Carolina A&T State University for the SAE International AutoDrive Challenge II, a competition in which university teams convert a production electric car into a self-driving vehicle. Tunji, a graduate of The Federal Polytechnic, Ilaro, Ogun State, serves as Electrical Engineer for Electric Vehicle Integration on the university’s team in Greensboro, North Carolina. The role covers the electrical systems on which the vehicle’s self-driving equipment depends. The power panel had been overheating, a fault that undermined the reliability of the vehicle’s electrical system. Tunji, it was gathered, led the reconstruction of the panel and coordinated the work with the team’s mechanical engineers. The rebuild eliminated the overheating and restored the reliability of the electrical system. “The repair carries more weight on a self-driving vehicle than on a conventional one. An autonomous car relies on sensors and onboard computers that need stable power for as long as the vehicle is in motion, so a fault in power distribution is a safety matter as well as a maintenance one,” Tunji said. The AutoDrive Challenge II is sponsored by SAE International, the engineering standards body, and General Motors. Ten universities in the United States and Canada were selected when the competition was announced in 2021. General Motors supplied each team with a Chevrolet Bolt EUV, an electric vehicle, as the base platform. The teams were asked to design and integrate their own autonomous driving systems, with the aim of navigating an urban driving course at Level 4 automation under the SAE J3016 standard. At that level, a vehicle is expected to drive itself within defined operating conditions without a human taking over. The teams meet for annual competitive events at vehicle test facilities in the United States. North Carolina A&T entered the second edition with a record from the first. Its team, Aggie Autonomous Auto, completed the original four-year AutoDrive Challenge in June 2021, and the university reported that the result earned it a place in the follow-on competition. Beyond the power panel, Tunji directed the design and implementation of a real-time blue-light safety alert for the vehicle. The system was built with the Python programming language and embedded systems, and was designed to improve the operational safety of the autonomous vehicle. He also produced the wiring diagrams and electrical subsystem documentation for the vehicle, prepared in line with SAE requirements so that the integration is safe and can be maintained. Such records matter on university teams, where members graduate and their successors must service systems they did not build. item.description: Smartphone cameras have become increasingly sophisticated in 2026, with manufacturers competing to deliver sharper photographs, improved low-light performance and, particularly, better zoom capabilities. One of the biggest developments has been the introduction of more advanced periscope telephoto cameras, larger image sensors and optical zoom systems capable of capturing distant subjects without relying entirely on digital enlargement. These improvements have made it possible to photograph wildlife, sporting events, concerts, buildings and other distant subjects with a level of detail that was previously difficult to achieve with a smartphone. While several manufacturers advertise zoom capabilities of up to 100x or 120x, the actual quality of photographs at those magnifications varies considerably. Optical zoom, sensor size, optical image stabilisation and image processing are therefore more important considerations than the maximum zoom figure alone. Here are five smartphones with some of the best zoom camera systems available in 2026, based on their camera hardware and independent reviews. 1. Oppo Find X9 Ultra The Oppo Find X9 Ultra stands out as one of the most capable zoom smartphones of 2026, particularly because it features two dedicated telephoto cameras rather than relying on a single zoom lens. The smartphone comes with a 200-megapixel primary telephoto camera offering 3x optical zoom and a separate 50-megapixel periscope telephoto camera capable of 10x optical zoom. The combination gives users greater flexibility when photographing subjects at different distances, from portraits and street photography to distant buildings, wildlife and performers at concerts. Its 10x optical zoom is particularly important because it allows the camera to magnify distant subjects using its dedicated optical hardware rather than simply enlarging pixels digitally. According to Digital Trends, the phone can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally. Its 200-megapixel telephoto camera also provides additional room for cropping images while retaining useful detail. The publication highlights the phone’s impressive telephoto sharpness, autofocus performance and ability to capture distant subjects. For people who regularly photograph sporting events, wildlife or concerts, the Find X9 Ultra is a particularly compelling option. 2. item.title: Disgruntled US tenant kills building manager, injures four, shoots self
item.description: A disgruntled tenant shot dead his building manager and wounded four other people in an upscale neighborhood of Washington on Thursday before killing himself, police said amid a massive law enforcement response that shut down part of the city. The shooting, which occurred about a mile north of the White House, sparked a massive police response in the nation’s capital with dozens of law enforcement vehicles racing to the scene and police helicopters hovering overhead. Dramatic dispatch audio captured the initial callout for a shooting inside the gym just before 8 am (0100 GMT). Within minutes a breathless police officer could be heard telling the dispatcher “we have an active shooter” and requesting the SWAT team. Jeffery Carroll, Washington’s interim police chief, told reporters that the gunman, identified as Matt Lambert, 55, had been involved in an ongoing dispute over maintenance with the condominium association for the building where he owned an apartment. Lambert, an emergency medicine physician, fatally shot the building manager, James Stuart, 46, in a packed gym attached to the complex, located in the Logan Circle neighborhood. Lambert then barricaded himself in his seventh-floor unit, Carroll said. He then opened fire from his balcony on people below, wounding four. One of the wounded was in critical condition while the others did not have life-threatening injuries. The Washington Post reported that construction workers from a nearby jobsite were among the injured, citing a company executive. Lambert fired at least twice at police through his apartment door and set the unit on fire before shooting himself, Carroll said. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Photos and video quickly emerged on social media of police in tactical gear surrounding the building with rifles drawn as well as fire emerging from an exterior wall. Carroll said Lambert had taken legal action against the homeowners association of the condominium complex where he lived over what he considered to be a lack of maintenance of the building. An X feed reportedly linked to Lambert titled @OfMiceandMold is a litany of complaints about mold and water damage. The final post, described as a “manifesto,” is an engineering report detailing problems with his apartment. Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser denounced what she described as a “senseless act of gun violence.” The shooting occurred during the busy morning rush hour, snarling traffic as police closed off streets around the area and evacuated residents. The Washington Sun quoted a member of the VIDA Fitness gym as saying that he was on a treadmill at the workout facility when the shooting began. Michael Carney said he heard a “pop” and then saw someone on the gym floor who had been shot in the head. “Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff,” Carney told The Sun. item.title: ‘Golden Ball Is My First Award in Life,’ Flamingos Star Umejiaku Relives World Cup Glory
item.description: Flamingos forward Oluebube Umejiaku has described her 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup Golden Ball award, following her performance and Nigeria’s triumph at the tournament, as her first in life. Speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Friday, Umejiaku, who said she was excited, noted that she had been praying for such recognition. “I feel very excited, and I give God all the glory because every day, I pray for it. That was my first award in life. “I am so happy that I got this award, and I give glory to God because it was not easy,” she said. ﻿ The forward noted that meeting with President Bola Tinubu, who was represented by his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, came to the players as an honour. “It was a great honour because everybody wanted to meet the President. We were very happy; we wanted to meet the President,” she said. “When we got there, the President was not around; we were happy to meet the First Lady.” Asked what came to mind when the President announced the financial reward, she said, “I was thinking about my mother; normally, I know that I don’t have access to the money.” She, however, said that she would invest in her future with the money. “By the special grace of God, I will like to see myself play for the Super Falcons and play for international clubs,” the striker said. “I will like to go far in life.” Umejiaku won the adidas Golden Ball at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, after scoring Nigeria’s second goal and helping the Flamingos claim their first title with a 2-1 victory over Japan in the final in Rabat. Her effort took her tally to four goals in the tournament. DPR Korea’s Yu Jong-hyang was awarded the Silver Ball, while Japan’s Fuki Ito got the Bronze Ball. United States forward Maddie DiMaria received the Golden Boot after finishing as the tournament’s top scorer with 12 goals. Yu Jong-hyang won the Silver Boot, while DPR Korea’s Ri Ui-gyong received the Bronze Boot. The Golden Glove for the goalkeeper of the tournament went to DPR Korea’s Kim Son-gyong, while Japan received the FIFA Fair Play Trophy. The performance of the Flamingos earned them commendation and a ₦100 million bond from President Tinubu at the Presidential Villa. They were also received by the Senate. item.title: US Lawmakers Summon Nvidia Ex-CEO After Affair With Suspected Spy
item.description: US lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters. “Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote Thursday on X. Scott said he was requesting Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs. It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena. Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related. US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations. On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell. While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. Nvidia hit gold when the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT in 2022 sparked a global rush to develop AI, with its processors — once designed for video game graphics — becoming a crucial ingredient to train and run the technology. Informal Trump Adviser Nvidia did not give a reason for the departure of Huang, who also gave up his board seat. Huang is Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder, with a stake of about 3.6 percent, according to the company. The Taiwanese-born businessman was a close informal adviser to President Donald Trump on AI, and had spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced AI chips to China for national security reasons. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives called it “a dark day for Nvidia and the US tech industry”. But he said the board had done what it needed: “rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him.” The board named Harvey Jones, a former chief executive of chip design software firm Synopsys, as chair, and said it expected the company’s operations and product roadmap “to continue without interruption.” Interim CEO Kress joined Nvidia in 2013 after nearly 25 years at companies including Cisco and Microsoft. item.title: Violent campaigns
item.description: Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, there are rising cases of political violence across Nigeria, despite efforts by various bodies to discourage mayhem before, during and after the polls. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Assembly elections have been slated for February 6, 2026. In the last seven days, there have been cases of political violence in no less than seven states, with the latest in Lagos, where several supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were injured after suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised on Thursday by the party for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. There was also an incident in Zamfara State during an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary. INEC will obey court verdict on Atiku’s eligibility – Amupitan How 4 UNN students died after graduation party Other states that recorded violence within the period included Edo, Delta, Gombe and Cross River states. The incidents have been more frequent this year, with states like Katsina, Kebbi, Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Ebonyi, Osun and Nasarawa states all experiencing various forms of political violence. Prominent political actors have also threatened voters in ways that raised concerns over free, fair and credible polls in 2027. The National Peace Committee revealed recently that reports spanning August 19 to October 27 documented 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also observed that political violence and thuggery led the violations with 33 incidents, closely followed by 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation and identified Kaduna, Edo, and Enugu as serious flashpoints for electoral violence. The European Union (EU) also expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of Nigeria’s general elections. EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, noted that these threats undermined democratic progress and discouraged citizens from participating freely in the electoral process. Daily Trust gathered that NDC supporters had arrived at the venue as early as 8am to prepare the hall ahead of the arrival of party leaders, including Obi and Kwankwaso, when the incident occurred. item.title: INEC Fixes Nov 28 For Nationwide Mock Accreditation Ahead Of 2027 General Elections
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has fixed November 28, 2026, for a nationwide mock accreditation exercise to test the effectiveness of its accreditation and electronic result transmission systems ahead of the 2027 general elections. ﻿ INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, announced this on Thursday in London during a high-level dialogue at Chatham House, organised in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI), under the theme, “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot.” Amupitan (right) spoke at Chatham House on Thursday, November 12, 2026. (Photo: X/@inecnigeria) Amupitan said that the exercise would simulate the presidential election and test the commission’s accreditation and electronic result transmission systems across all states of the federation. “On the 28th of this month, we will conduct a mock accreditation across all states of the federation to simulate the presidential election and verify that we have gotten both accreditation and electronic result transmission right,” he said. The INEC chairman, who is a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, further stated that the exercise was part of measures to address technical challenges experienced during the 2023 general elections and strengthen the credibility of the 2027 polls. He disclosed that the commission had procured extra devices and reduced the maximum number of voters assigned to each BVAS machine from 1,250 to 850. According to him, polling units with more than 850 registered voters will be provided with multiple devices. Amupitan also said INEC was constructing climate-controlled storage facilities in all states to address the malfunction of BVAS devices previously linked to extreme heat and storage conditions during the 2023 elections. On electronic result transmission, he explained that the commission had introduced technical safeguards to prevent inaccurate results and figures reflecting over-voting from being uploaded to its Result Viewing Portal (IReV). He identified insecurity, logistics and result management as the commission’s three major priorities ahead of the 2027 elections. The INEC chairman said a post-2023 audit showed that the most significant failures in result management occurred at collation centres rather than polling units. He added that the commission had opted to upgrade its existing electoral technology rather than introduce an entirely new system because of the limited time before the 2027 elections. Amupitan also confirmed that INEC had received a substantial portion of its 2027 election budget but was awaiting the outstanding balance, part of which would fund the recruitment and welfare of ad hoc personnel. He said the commission had received assurances that the outstanding funds would be released before the end of November.
